Anglet aligne onze plages de surf sur qu: Anglet has eleven surf beaches along a few kilometers of coastline, separated by jetties: a playground where each beach has its own vibe.
Annexes et bateaux nombreux au mouillage: Lots of boats and moorings in the bay: make sure you’re clearly visible when swimming, ideally with a buoy.
Anse de sable blanc et d’eau turquoise s: A white-sand cove with turquoise water on the east coast of Espiritu Santo, near Hog Harbour. It gets its name from the small bubbles of volcanic origin that sometimes rise from the sand at low tide.

Arche naturelle d’environ 54 m de haut q: A natural arch about 54 m high that spans the Ardèche at the entrance to the gorges. It’s a landmark on the classic canoe and kayak route, with large pebble beaches for swimming.
Arches et piliers de roche volcanique bl: White volcanic rock arches and pillars on the southwest coast of Milos, once a pirate hideout. You can only get there by boat or sea kayak.
Archipel caribéen aux cabanes sur piloti: A Caribbean archipelago with overwater huts, reef waves and mangroves. A laid-back, wild vibe.
Archipel de cayes, de mangroves et de ré: An archipelago of cays, mangroves and reefs off Cuba’s south coast, a national park since 2010. Diving is only allowed from authorised liveaboards, with visitor numbers limited.
Archipel de centaines d’îlots de sable e: An archipelago of hundreds of sandy islets and coconut palms on Panama’s Caribbean coast, in Guna territory (formerly called San Blas). The Chichimé cays, among the most visited, offer turquoise water and shallow reefs.
Archipel de granit au cœur de la réserve: A granite archipelago at the heart of the Bouches de Bonifacio Nature Reserve, accessible by boat from Bonifacio. Its turquoise coves are great for snorkelling, and divers come for the groupers.
Archipel de neuf îlots protégé en réserv: An archipelago of nine protected islets in a nature reserve, about 20 km offshore, northwest of Muscat. Its reefs are home to turtles, rays and, in season, whale sharks.
Archipel de récifs coralliens au sud-oue: Coral reef archipelago southwest of Cartagena, within the Corales del Rosario y de San Bernardo National Park. Warm, clear waters for snorkelling, accessible by boat on a day trip.
Archipel de sable blanc et de lagons tur: A white-sand archipelago with turquoise lagoons, protected as a national park. One of the Caribbean’s most beautiful lagoons.
Archipel du détroit de Taïwan balayé par: An archipelago in the Taiwan Strait swept by the northeast monsoon from October to March. Aimen Beach, on the main island, is one of Asia’s best-known windsurfing and kitesurfing spots.
Archipel isolé : soins médicaux limités,: Remote archipelago: medical care is limited, so find out about evacuations.
Archipel où les baleines à bosse viennen: An archipelago where humpback whales come to give birth. One of the few places where you can swim with them.
Archipel protégé par un parc national au: An archipelago protected by a national park off the Mekong Delta. Around Hòn Bảy Cạnh, you can explore coral reefs and green turtle nesting beaches with authorised operators.
Argenté et massif, il remonte respirer à: Large and silvery, it comes to the surface to breathe.

Atolls et lagons peu profonds, sur fond: Atolls and shallow lagoons over white coral sand.
Atolls isolés en pleine mer de Sulu, cla: Remote atolls in the middle of the Sulu Sea, listed as a World Heritage Site. Accessible only on a liveaboard trip from March to June.

Au débouché du Verdon, un vaste lac s’ét: Where the Verdon opens out, a vast lake stretches between the Var and Alpes-de-Haute-Provence. Its shores offer starting points for kayaking or paddleboarding from authorized access points.
Au large de Capbreton s'ouvre le Gouf, u: Off Capbreton lies the Gouf, an underwater canyon more than 3000 m deep that begins a few hundred meters from shore.
Au large de Perth, Wadjemup — Rottnest I: Off Perth, Wadjemup — Rottnest Island — has beaches, bays and reefs. Plan an Australian stop around snorkeling, diving or kayaking.
Au large de Saint-Jean-de-Luz, la vague: Off Saint-Jean-de-Luz, the giant Belharra wave was surfed for the first time on 22 November 2002 by a handful of surfers, including Peyo Lizarazu. Breaking about 2.5 km from shore and reaching 8 to 15 m, it put the Basque Country on the world big-wave map.
Au large de la pointe sud de Yonaguni, î: Off the southern tip of Yonaguni, Japan’s westernmost island, underwater rock terraces intrigue divers. In winter, hammerhead sharks can also be spotted offshore.
Au large du sud du Vietnam, Phú Quốc réu: Off southern Vietnam, Phú Quốc has beaches and nearby islets. Choose snorkeling and diving trips with local centers according to the area and weather.
Au nord de Durban, Umhlanga mêle plage,: North of Durban, Umhlanga combines beach, promenade and surfing on the KwaZulu-Natal coast. A seaside stop for exploring the region.
Au nord de La Paz, Balandra réunit une b: North of La Paz, Balandra has a bay, beaches and a landscape of desert hills. It’s a kayaking stop in a protected natural area; check access arrangements before visiting.
Au nord de Palawan, El Nido ouvre sur l’: North of Palawan, El Nido opens onto the Bacuit Archipelago. You can explore its limestone cliffs, bays and lagoons on boat or kayak trips, or while snorkeling.
Au nord de l’île du Sud, le parc nationa: At the north of the South Island, Abel Tasman National Park borders a series of wooded bays. Kayak trips connect some of the beaches and combine paddling with coastal walks.
Au nord du Yucatán, Holbox sépare le gol: North of the Yucatán, Holbox separates the Gulf of Mexico from a coastal lagoon. The island is suited to a beach, kayaking and kitesurfing trip with local providers.
Au nord tropical d'octobre à mai : combi: In the tropical north from October to May: a protective jellyfish suit is mandatory.
Au nord-est de Bali, Amed désigne un ens: In northeastern Bali, Amed refers to a group of coastal villages, including Jemeluk and Lipah. Plan snorkeling and diving bay by bay with local centers.
Au nord-ouest de Praslin, une plage bord: Northwest of Praslin, Anse Lazio is a beach lined with vegetation and granite rocks. It’s a Seychelles stop for enjoying the shore and exploring the seabed close to it.
Au pied de la Serra da Arrábida, une pet: At the foot of the Serra da Arrábida, a small bay opens between wooded hills and the sea. The coast is part of a protected area: plan access and your outing with local operators.
Au pied du cap de Point Lookout, Main Be: At the foot of Point Lookout headland, Main Beach stretches along a long beach exposed to Pacific swell. The headland offers several aspects: the more sheltered Cylinder Beach is better suited to beginners.

Au sud de Nouméa, la baie de l’Anse Vata: South of Nouméa, Anse Vata Bay is a windsurfing destination. The seafront looks out over the lagoon and Îlot Canard; plan your route with local clubs.
Au sud de Taghazout, Tamraght offre un p: South of Taghazout, Tamraght is a starting point for exploring the coast and its surf spots with local schools.
Au sud de Tamarindo, une autre plage de: South of Tamarindo lies another Guanacaste surf beach, a stop along Nicoya’s coastal route.

Baie abritée au sud-est de l’île, au cœu: A sheltered bay in the southeast of the island, at the heart of Mafia Island Marine Park, with coral reefs, seagrass beds and dive passages. Whale sharks visit the west coast near Kilindoni in season, especially from October to March.

Baie au sable le plus blanc du monde, di: A bay said to have the whitest sand in the world, with dolphins and a marine park. Calm, clear water.
Baie connue pour ses tortues vertes et,: A bay known for its green turtles and, sometimes, a dugong grazing on the seagrass. Snorkel from the beach.
Baie de False Bay : respecte les consign: False Bay: follow the shark monitoring team’s instructions.
Baie de Gallura, au nord de la Sardaigne: Bay of Gallura, in northern Sardinia, split in two by the sandy isthmus of Isola dei Gabbiani. Winds funnelled through the Strait of Bonifacio make it one of the Mediterranean’s best-known windsurfing and kitesurfing spots.
Baie de Hainan qui accueille des compéti: A Hainan bay that hosts international competitions and surf schools. Surfing is growing in China here.
Baie de Sal Rei, abritée par l’îlot du m: Bay of Sal Rei, sheltered by the islet of the same name, where northeast trade winds blow mostly in winter and spring. In front of Estoril Beach, kite and windsurf schools make the most of water that’s often calmer near shore.
Baie de San Fruttuoso, sur le promontoir: San Fruttuoso Bay, on the Portofino promontory, accessible only by sea or on foot. Offshore from the beach, a bronze statue of Christ rests in about 17 m of water within the marine protected area.
Baie de la côte ouest de Maurice, avec u: A bay on Mauritius’s west coast, with a reef left and dolphins in the morning. Famous for its sunsets.
Baie de la presqu’île de la Caravelle, p: A bay on the Caravelle peninsula, near the village of Tartane, exposed to Atlantic swell. It’s one of Martinique’s best-known surf spots, with several surf schools.
Baie de sable peu profonde au sud de Var: A shallow sandy bay south of Varberg, on Sweden’s west coast. A family-friendly beach in calm weather, it becomes one of Sweden’s best-known windsurfing and kitesurfing spots when the westerly wind picks up, with surfable waves at times.
Baie de sable sombre au pied des colline: A dark-sand bay at the foot of the hills, near Soufrière, in the protected marine area off Saint Lucia’s west coast. The reef starts just in front of the beach, then drops away.
Baie de sable sur la côte ouest de Phuke: A sandy bay on Phuket’s west coast. Calm in the dry season, it gets surfable waves during the southwest monsoon, roughly from May to October.
Baie du nord du Devon réputée pour ses v: A North Devon bay known for its hollow waves at low tide. The heart of English surfing, with the villages of Saunton and Woolacombe.
Baie du nord du Guanacaste, près de la f: A bay in northern Guanacaste, near the Nicaraguan border, swept by steady winds during the dry season. Kite schools based on the beach make the most of water that’s often fairly flat inside the bay.
Baie du nord-ouest de Maui, protégée en: A bay in northwest Maui, protected as a marine reserve. In winter, a powerful right-hand reef break peels off beneath the point and draws advanced surfers; in summer, the calm bay becomes a renowned snorkelling spot.
Baie du sud de Lefkada où un vent thermi: A bay in southern Lefkada where a steady thermal wind picks up almost every summer afternoon. Calm mornings for learning, stronger afternoons for advanced riders: a European windsurfing classic.
Baie désertique au vent régulier, près d: A desert bay with steady wind, near the national reserve and the Ballestas Islands. A kite spot in the middle of the desert.
Baie en arc de cercle au pied des montag: A crescent-shaped bay at the foot of Kauaʻi’s mountains. Calm for paddleboarding in summer, powerful for surfing in winter.
Baie en arc de cercle au sud de Porto-Ve: A crescent-shaped bay south of Porto-Vecchio, with white sand and very shallow turquoise water. Perfect for families, paddleboarding or kayaking, with a few rocks to explore from the headlands with a mask.
Baie en arc de cercle bordée de cocotier: A crescent-shaped bay lined with coconut palms in southern Goa. Outside the monsoon, the water is calm and ideal for swimming and kayaking to the rocks and the islet at the north end of the beach.
Baie en arc parfait dans le parc nationa: A perfectly crescent-shaped bay in Freycinet National Park, at the foot of the Hazards’ granite mountains. You can reach it on foot from the lookout car park or by sea kayak from Coles Bay with a guide.
Baie en fer à cheval à la pointe nord-ou: A horseshoe-shaped bay at the northwest tip of Mahé, protected as a national marine park. Coral, turtles and reef fish can be spotted close to shore, often on boat trips.
Baie nord pour naviguer, baie sud pour n: North bay for sailing, south bay for swimming: the headland really separates the two.
Baie presque fermée en forme de coquilla: A nearly enclosed, shell-shaped bay between Porto-Vecchio and Bonifacio. Shallow turquoise water, ideal for families and paddleboarding.
Baie protégée où des centaines de raies: A protected bay where hundreds of manta rays gather to feed from June to November. A biosphere reserve.
Baie reconnue comme l’une des plus biolu: A bay known as one of the world’s most bioluminescent: at night, every paddle stroke lights up the water blue thanks to microscopic plankton. You can visit by kayak with authorised guides.

Longue plage de sable doré sur la côte e: A long golden-sand beach on Paros’s east coast, exposed to the meltemi that often blows in summer. Several windsurfing and kitesurfing schools are based here.

Longue plage de sable fin sur la rive fr: A long fine-sand beach on the French shore of Lake Geneva, one of the lake’s few natural sandy beaches. The seabed slopes gently, perfect for swimming and paddleboarding.
Longue plage de sable sombre face au Pac: A long dark-sand beach facing the Pacific, often described as the birthplace of Philippine surfing. The beach break is accessible to beginners in small swell, especially from autumn to spring.

Petit port du sud d’El Hierro, porte d’e: Small harbour in southern El Hierro, gateway to the La Restinga – Mar de las Calmas marine reserve. Volcanic drop-offs, arches and clear water make it one of the Canary Islands' best-known diving destinations.
Petit village de la côte du Piauí, entre: Small village on the coast of Piauí, between the Parnaíba Delta and Ceará, now a renowned kitesurfing spot. At low tide, large areas of shallow, flat water make it a calm place to learn.
Petit village de pêcheurs au nord d’Essa: Small fishing village north of Essaouira, among Africa's best-known wave windsurfing spots. The strong northeasterly trade wind in summer blows side-shore over powerful waves.
Petite anse de pêcheurs où les tortues b: Small fishing cove where turtles graze on seagrass just a few metres from shore. An almost guaranteed encounter.
Petite anse de sable et de blocs de gran: Small cove of sand and granite boulders on the northeast shore of Lake Tahoe, at nearly 1,900 m elevation. The water is exceptionally clear, and the sheltered coves are perfect for paddleboarding and kayaking in calm weather.
Petite baie abritée près de Royan, vague: Small sheltered bay near Royan, with gentle waves ideal for learning. Beach resort feel and often calm water.
Petite baie au sud-ouest de Pangandaran,: Small bay southwest of Pangandaran, sheltered by a rocky headland. The right-hand wave rolls gently over a sandy, rocky bottom, making this one of Java's best-known spots for learning to surf.
Petite baie de Lifou où le récif coralli: Small bay on Lifou where the coral reef starts at the foot of the cliff, near the village of Easo. Its crystal-clear water makes it one of the Loyalty Islands' best-known snorkelling spots.
Petite baie de galets du San Juan County: Small pebble bay in San Juan County Park, on the island's west coast, a classic starting point for sea-kayaking trips to Haro Strait. In summer, orcas often swim along the shore.
Petite baie de la côte nord-est jamaïcai: Small bay on Jamaica's northeast coast, one of the island's historic surf spots. The village is also known as the birthplace of jerk, Jamaica's spicy cuisine.
Petite baie de sable blanc et d’eau turq: Small bay of white sand and turquoise water south of Coquimbo, framed by rocks. Local surfers know it for its waves over rocky bottoms when the swell comes in, and for its clear water when the sea is calm.
Petite baie du parc marin de Hoi Ha Wan,: Small bay in Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park, north of the Sai Kung Peninsula. Despite being so close to the city, it is home to dozens of hard coral species.
Petite baie du sud du Sri Lanka, avec un: Small bay in southern Sri Lanka, with a reef break at its western end and a sheltered beach in the dry season. It's also the main departure harbour for blue whale-watching trips.
Petite baie en fer à cheval bordée de ro: Small horseshoe-shaped bay lined with rocks, on the coast between Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo. In calm seas, you can set off straight from the beach with a mask and snorkel to spot reef fish.
Petite baie tropicale bordée de cocotier: Small tropical bay lined with coconut palms, a pioneer of surfing in Ghana. Gentle waves ideal for learning.
Petite crique de galets du parc national: Small pebble cove in Channel Islands National Park, where boats from Ventura come ashore. Nearby cliffs are riddled with sea caves to explore by kayak, and the kelp draws fish close to shore.
Petite crique de galets encaissée entre: Small pebble cove nestled between the limestone cliffs of Polignano a Mare, beneath an old stone bridge. The old town perched above the water makes it one of the most photographed beaches in Puglia.
Petite crique de sable blanc entourée d’: Small white-sand cove surrounded by dark serpentinite islets on the Lizard Peninsula. At low tide, the turquoise water and rocks invite you to enjoy a peaceful swim and a bit of snorkelling.
Petite crique encadrée de falaises, où l: Small cove framed by cliffs, where turtles come to feed. Easy, spectacular snorkelling.
Petite crique encaissée entre George et: Small cove nestled between George and Wilderness, with a tiny beach and a famous point break on the South Coast. The wave peels along the rocks and works with a south-west swell.
Petite plage au pied de l’église Saint-J: Small beach below the Church of St. John at Kaneo, perched on the rocks by Lake Ohrid. One of Europe’s oldest and deepest lakes, listed by UNESCO, with clear waters and many endemic species.
Petite plage de la côte est de Miyako, o: Small beach on the east coast of Miyako, where the coral reef starts just a few metres from shore. A classic spot for easy snorkelling among reef fish.
Petite plage à l’extrémité est d’Ipanema: Small beach at the eastern end of Ipanema, below the Arpoador rock. The birthplace of surfing in Rio, it offers a wave along the rock and a very lively beach break.
Petite station balnéaire Belle Époque pr: Small Belle Époque seaside resort near Boulogne, with a pebble and sand beach, great for kitesurfing and lifeguarded swimming.
Petite vague abritée idéale pour apprend: Small sheltered wave ideal for learning in often calm water. Beautiful Breton setting, perfect for families and first sessions.
Petite ville historique de Basse-Califor: Small historic town in Baja California facing the islands of Loreto Bay National Marine Park. By kayak or boat, you can reach coves where you might spot sea lions, pelicans and sometimes dolphins.
Petite île au sud de Sainte-Marie, entou: Small island south of Sainte-Marie, surrounded by a clear lagoon and white-sand beaches. From July to September, humpback whales pass through the channel between Sainte-Marie and Grande Terre.
Petite île classée monument naturel, à e: Small island designated a natural monument, about 2 km off the coast of La Romana. Its best-known sites are “The Wall”, a drop-off for divers, and “The Aquarium”, a shallow reef for snorkelling.
Petite île corallienne au large de Pangl: Small coral island off Panglao, surrounded by a marine sanctuary. The reef flat and drop-off are home to turtles, schools of trevally and healthy corals.
Petite île corallienne tout au sud de la: Small coral island at the southern tip of the Great Barrier Reef, surrounded by a reef you can reach from the beach. The lagoon is ideal for a relaxed snorkel, and manta rays are often spotted around the island.
Petite île sans voiture entourée de réci: Small car-free island surrounded by reefs and turtles. Laid-back atmosphere and dives for all levels.
Petites criques abritées entre d’énormes: Sheltered coves between huge granite boulders in Table Mountain National Park, home to a colony of African penguins. False Bay’s calm water is good for swimming, but it’s still chilly.
Petites forêts brunes des zones battues,: Small brown seaweed forests in wave-exposed areas, in sharp decline in the Canary Islands.

Plage au pied des falaises de Sagres, to: Beach below the cliffs of Sagres, at the very edge of Europe. Exposed to the west, it gets swell when the south coast is flat.
Plage de 5 km à São Sebastião, sur le li: 5 km beach in São Sebastião, on the northern coast of the state of São Paulo. Its powerful waves and currents make it one of Brazil’s best-known spots, regularly hosting competitions.
Plage de Kyushu aux vagues régulières, q: Kyushu beach with consistent waves, which has hosted world surfing championships. Relaxed Japanese atmosphere.
Plage de galets au sud de l’archipel de: Pebble beach south of the Stockholm archipelago, exposed to the open Baltic Sea. Autumn and winter storms bring short, powerful waves, making it the best-known surf spot on Sweden’s east coast.
Plage de galets blancs au pied de falais: White pebble beach at the foot of limestone cliffs on the northwest coast of Kefalonia. The turquoise water gets deep very quickly.
Plage de galets en plein cœur de la vill: Pebble beach in the heart of town, a well-known kitesurfing spot with small waves on a south-west swell.
Plage de galets et de sable sombre de la: Pebble and dark-sand beach on the coast of La Libertad, known for its pig-shaped rock, “el tunco”. Several rocky and pebble-bottom peaks follow one after another, with Sunzal’s right just next door.
Plage de galets et point break de la côt: Pebble beach and point break on Canada’s Atlantic coast. You can surf even in winter, in a thick wetsuit.
Plage de galets et rochers glissants à l: Pebble beach with slippery rocks at the water’s edge.
Plage de la côte est coréenne, au cœur d: Beach on Korea’s east coast, at the heart of Yangyang’s surf scene, with its schools and cafés. Waves in the East Sea are small in summer and more consistent in autumn and winter.
Plage de la côte nord de Kauaʻi, bordée: Beach on Kauaʻi’s north shore, edged by a wide fringing reef carved with arches and tunnels. In calm seas, especially in summer, it’s one of the island’s best spots for snorkelling and shore diving.
Plage de la pointe sud-est d’Oahu, célèb: Beach at the southeastern tip of Oahu, famous for its shore break that crashes straight onto the sand. It’s a favourite bodyboarding and bodysurfing spot for experienced locals, but also one of the island’s most accident-prone beaches.
Plage de la première ville au monde à vo: Beach in the world’s first city to see the sunrise. Consistent beach break and a laid-back vibe.
Plage de la presqu’île de Giens réputée: Beach on the Giens peninsula, renowned across Europe for dinghy sailing. The mistral and easterly winds often blow here over turquoise water.
Plage de la rive est du lac de Neusiedl,: Beach on the eastern shore of Lake Neusiedl, a vast, very shallow steppe lake. You can stand far from shore, making it an ideal spot to learn windsurfing and kitesurfing, and a major hub for Austrian board sports.
Plage de la réserve marine de Cape Rodne: Beach in the Cape Rodney-Okakari Point Marine Reserve, facing Goat Island. Decades of protection have brought large fish back close to shore: you can spot them just metres from the beach with a mask and snorkel.
Plage de sable au confluent du fjord du: Sandy beach where the Saguenay Fjord meets the St. Lawrence River, in Saguenay–St. Lawrence Marine Park. Kayaks are launched here to paddle along the headlands and, with luck, spot belugas and minke whales.
Plage de sable blanc au bord d’un grand: White-sand beach beside a large, shallow lagoon on the southern Atlantic coast of Martinique. The steady trade winds and sandy bottom make it a popular spot for learning to kitesurf and windsurf.
Plage de sable blanc au fond d’un fjord,: White-sand beach at the head of a fjord, surrounded by mountains. A spectacular Arctic surf spot, sheltered from the wind.
Plage de sable blanc de Whitesand Bay, t: White-sand beach at Whitesand Bay, close to Land’s End at the western tip of Cornwall. It catches almost every Atlantic swell: gentle waves near the harbour, with stronger surf at the north end of the bay.
Plage de sable blanc du Parc national de: White-sand beach in Port-Cros National Park, at the back of a pine-fringed bay. The crystal-clear water is perfect for snorkelling over the seagrass beds.
Plage de sable blanc du parc national de: White-sand beach in Cape Range National Park, where Ningaloo Reef starts just a few metres from shore. It’s known for its “drift snorkel”: let the current carry you along the reef.
Plage de sable blanc et d’eau turquoise: White-sand beach with turquoise water, where kangaroos sometimes come down onto the sand.
Plage de sable blanc et pins parasols au: White-sand beach with umbrella pines and turquoise water, one of Corsica’s most beautiful: swimming and snorkelling.
Plage de sable blanc longue de plusieurs: Several-kilometre-long white-sand beach on the east coast of Niijima, one of the Izu Islands administered by Tokyo. Exposed to Pacific swell, it regularly hosts surf competitions.
Plage de sable blanc sur la côte au vent: White-sand beach on Oahu’s windward coast, with the Mokuluas islets offshore. A paradise for kayaking and kitesurfing.
Plage de sable blanc sur la côte nord-ou: White-sand beach on Zanzibar’s northwest coast, where the sea doesn’t recede as far as it does on the island’s east coast, so you can swim at almost any time. Snorkelling boat trips leave from the nearby coast.
Plage de sable blanc à la pointe est d’U: White-sand beach at the eastern tip of Upolu, facing the islet of Nuʻutele and lined with traditional fale. The clear lagoon is perfect for swimming and snorkelling.
Plage de sable corallien bordée de cocot: Coral-sand beach lined with coconut palms and moai, in the north of Easter Island. One of the island’s few beaches.
Plage de sable d’une douzaine de kilomèt: Around a dozen-kilometre-long sandy beach in southern Montenegro, stretching to the mouth of the Bojana. The afternoon thermal wind makes it the country’s main kitesurfing spot.
Plage de sable encadrée de collines bois: Sandy beach framed by wooded hills north of San Juan del Sur. Thanks to nearby Lake Nicaragua, the wind often blows offshore, keeping the waves clean for much of the year.
Plage de sable et de galets au pied de h: Sand-and-pebble beach at the foot of high white cliffs, southwest of Lefkada. You can reach it down a long staircase or by boat from Nydri and Vassiliki.
Plage de sable noir à l’ouest de Honiara: Black-sand beach west of Honiara, in front of two Japanese transport shipwrecks sunk during the 1942 Battle of Guadalcanal. You can explore them from shore: one wreck’s upper section breaks the surface, while the other lies much deeper.
Plage de sable quartzeux très fin qui cr: Beach of very fine quartz sand that squeaks underfoot, framed by huge orange granite boulders in Wilsons Promontory National Park. The water is clear but cool.
Plage de sable très fin face à l’îlot de: Beach of very fine sand facing the islet of La Pelosa and its Aragonese tower, at the northwest tip of Sardinia. Its shallow turquoise water makes it a family-friendly beach, protected by strict rules.
Plage de sable volcanique dominée par un: Volcanic-sand beach overlooked by a solidified lava flow in Cabo de Gata-Níjar Natural Park. The rocks at either end are great for snorkelling.
Plage de surf exposée de Phillip Island,: Exposed surf beach on Phillip Island, taking the full force of swell from Bass Strait. The waves are often powerful, and the beach has a reputation as one of the most dangerous in Victoria.
Plage du nord-ouest de Porto Rico, connu: Beach in northwest Puerto Rico, known for its right that peels along the reef. It’s lively on shore, with restaurants and bars facing the water.
Plage du parc de la Serra do Tabuleiro q: Beach in Serra do Tabuleiro Park, reached by crossing the Rio da Madre on foot or by boat. The sandbanks at the river mouth create a renowned wave, one of the best known in Santa Catarina.
Plage du parc national des Îles Vierges,: Beach in Virgin Islands National Park, known for its marked underwater trail around Trunk Cay. The white sand and clear water make it one of the most photographed beaches in the Caribbean.
Plage du sud de Mayotte, célèbre pour se: Beach in southern Mayotte, famous for its green turtles grazing on seagrass just a few metres from shore. Easy snorkelling in the lagoon at the foot of Mount Choungui.
Plage du sud de Taïwan aux vagues réguli: Beach in southern Taiwan with consistent waves, at the edge of Kenting National Park.
Plage d’accès de Ngor ; le reef de Ngor: Ngor access beach; the Ngor Right reef is offshore.
Plage en arc de cercle d’environ 1,6 km: Curved beach about 1.6 km long on Culebra Island, with turquoise water sheltered at the back of its bay. Rusting old tanks recall the time when the US Navy used the island for training exercises.
Plage encadrée de collines vertes au nor: Beach framed by green hills north of Garopaba, one of the top surf spots in southern Brazil. Waves peel over the sandbanks and along the rocky point.
Plage entourée de collines et de rochers: Beach surrounded by hills and rocks, with powerful waves. One of the standout spots on Santa Catarina Island.
Plage entourée de forêt atlantique, avec: Beach surrounded by Atlantic Forest, with a river flowing into the ocean. Ubatuba’s most consistent spot.
Plage exposée aux alizés de l’Atlantique: Beach exposed to the Atlantic trade winds, east of Santa Maria. A spot with steady wind from November to May.
Plage face à la montagne de la Table, my: Beach facing Table Mountain, legendary for kitesurfing in the waves. The southeasterly blows hard here in summer.
Plage familiale aux vagues douces, parfa: Family beach with gentle waves, perfect for learning. Often calm water and surf schools nearby.
Plage iconique aux blocs de granit rose: Iconic beach with pink granite boulders and a shallow lagoon protected by the reef: picture-postcard swimming and snorkelling.
Plage immense balayée par le vent, haut: Huge windswept beach, a hotspot for kite flying and kitesurfing, with seals in the nearby Bay of Authie.
Plage isolée au fond de la baie de Corri: Secluded beach at the back of Corrientes Bay, at the westernmost tip of Cuba, on the Guanahacabibes Peninsula, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Coral drop-offs start just a few minutes by boat from the dive centre.

Plage préservée avec une immense dune et: Unspoilt beach backed by a huge dune and Roman ruins, facing Morocco. The Strait’s levant and poniente winds make this a powerful wind sports spot.
Plage sauvage adossée à la Serra de Sint: Wild beach backed by the Serra de Sintra, battered by the northerly wind for most of the summer. A go-to spot for kiting and windsurfing in strong winds.
Plage sauvage au bout d’une piste de sab: Wild beach at the end of a sandy track, in the heart of the Camargue. A legendary, isolated, flat water sports spot for both the mistral and sea breezes.
Plage sauvage du sud de Mahé, bordée de: Wild beach in southern Mahé, fringed with granite and coconut palms, with no reef offshore. It picks up Indian Ocean swell and has one of the island’s few surfable waves, especially from May to October.

Viens autour de la marée haute et prévoi: Come around high tide and wear water shoes for the walk across the channel.
Viens avec quelqu’un et évite de te baig: Come with someone and avoid swimming when there’s swell: this beach is better suited to surfing than swimming.
Viens avec une <b>gourde réutilisable</b: Bring a reusable water bottle instead of a plastic one.
Viens de novembre à avril : pendant la m: Come from November to April: during the southwest monsoon, the sea gets rough and crossings are choppier.
Viens de novembre à avril ; pour les bal: Come from November to April; for whale watching, choose an operator that respects approach distances.
Viens en juillet-août, quand le parcours: Come in July–August, when the route is marked and supervised; wear water shoes in the water, as the pebbles are slippery.
Viens en saison sèche, environ de décemb: Come in the dry season, roughly December to April, and ask the schools about sailing areas.
Viens entre mai et septembre, quand la c: Come between May and September, when the east coast is calm, and arrive early: the site gets very busy in the afternoon.
Viens entre mars et octobre : pendant la: Come between March and October: during the northeast monsoon, the sea is rough and many accommodations close.
Viens entre novembre et mars ; pendant l: Come between November and March; during the monsoon (June to September), the sea is rough and swimming is often prohibited.
Viens par vent faible de secteur sud-oue: Come when there’s a light southwesterly wind: easterly or northerly winds make the water cloudy.
Viens plutôt à marée haute : à marée bas: Come at high tide if you can: at low tide, the reef flat is exposed and you have to go farther out to swim over the corals.
Viens surfer avec une gourde réutilisabl: Bring a reusable water bottle when you surf.
Viens tôt : le sentier est court mais ra: Come early: the trail is short but steep, and boats arrive in the late morning.
Viens tôt avant que le vent ne se lève e: Come early before the wind picks up, and follow the rules set by the community that manages beach access.
Viens tôt le matin : la crique est minus: Come early in the morning: the cove is tiny and fills up fast in summer.
Viens tôt le matin en été, avant l’arriv: Come early in the morning in summer, before the boats and crowds arrive.
Viens tôt le matin ou en fin d’après-mid: Come early in the morning or late afternoon: the site gets packed when cruise ships are in port.
Viens à l’aube ou hors saison : la criqu: Come at dawn or out of season: the cove is tiny and packed in summer.
Viens à l’ouverture pour profiter du cal: Come at opening time to enjoy the quiet, rinse off before going in, and skip the sunscreen: it damages the cenote water.
Viens à l’étale de marée pour une eau pl: Come at slack tide for clearer water and weaker currents, and stay outside the hulls.
Viens à marée basse : à marée haute la p: Come at low tide: at high tide, the beach almost disappears. The car park fills up early in summer.
Viens à marée haute et en semaine ; pêch: Come at high tide and on weekdays; fishing and collecting are prohibited in the marine park.
Vient brouter les herbiers du lagon à ma: Comes to graze on the lagoon's seagrass beds at high tide.
Vient mettre bas d'août à novembre au la: Comes to give birth off Abrolhos from August to November.
Vient mettre bas près du bord de juin à: Comes to give birth near shore from June to November.
Vient se chauffer à plat en surface les: Comes to bask flat at the surface on calm days: impressive but harmless.
Vient se reproduire dans le golfe Nuevo: Comes to breed in Golfo Nuevo from June to December.
Village accroché à une falaise au bord d: Village perched on a cliff above the Dordogne, listed among France’s Most Beautiful Villages. You can canoe down the river at the foot of the castles of Castelnaud and Beynac.
Village aux portes des dunes blanches et: Village on the doorstep of the white dunes and freshwater lagoons of the Lençóis. Kitesurf at the river mouth.
Village de Chembe, dans le parc national: Village of Chembe, in Lake Malawi National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its clear freshwater is home to hundreds of colorful cichlid species, which you can observe by kayak or snorkel around the islets.
Village de dunes classé, vent quasi quot: A village among protected dunes, with near-daily wind and lagoons: one of Brazil's most famous kite spots.
Village de kite au vent régulier, à côté: Kitesurfing village with steady wind, near Jericoacoara. Lagoons and ocean for all levels.
Village de la Costa dos Coqueiros, au no: Village on the Costa dos Coqueiros, north of Salvador, home to a base for the TAMAR sea turtle conservation project. At low tide, the reefs form natural pools that are perfect for snorkelling.
Village de la Wild Coast niché dans une: Wild Coast village nestled in a bay between green hills, with a sandy beach at the river mouth. The beach breaks suit self-sufficient surfers, and the famous Hole in the Wall is a few kilometres down the coast.
Village de la côte Pacifique de Veraguas: Village on the Pacific coast of Veraguas known for its point break over volcanic rock, offering both rights and lefts when the swell is good. It’s also the departure port for Coiba National Park.
Village de la côte de Sligo connu pour s: Village on the Sligo coast known for its two reef breaks, a left and a right, peeling over rock slabs on either side of the river mouth. A historic Irish surf spot.
Village de la mer de Cortés où souffle u: Sea of Cortez village with steady northerly wind from November to March. A North American kitesurfing favourite.
Village de la presqu’île de Hel bordé pa: Village on the Hel Peninsula, bordered by Puck Bay, a shallow, flat body of water that’s popular for learning to kitesurf and windsurf. Schools line the bay side of the campsites.
Village de plongée au nord de Mindoro, f: Dive village north of Mindoro, facing Verde Island Passage, known for its remarkable variety of coastal fish. Reefs, submerged wrecks and steep drop-offs line the coast.
Village de plongée sur la deuxième plus: Dive village on the world’s second-largest barrier reef. Affordable diving and reefs just metres from shore.
Village de pêcheurs au nord de Perth, pr: Fishing village north of Perth, sheltered by a reef barrier and islets. The afternoon sea breeze is reliable during the austral summer, making it a major windsurfing and kitesurfing destination.
Village de pêcheurs au nord-ouest de Fue: Fishing village in northwest Fuerteventura, with powerful beach breaks to the south and calm lagoons to the north. Two different vibes in one day.
Village de pêcheurs au sud de Chennai, d: Fishing village south of Chennai, now Tamil Nadu’s best-known surf spot. The rocky point and beach break offer waves that are often modest, making them good for learning.
Village de pêcheurs de la côte Pacifique: Fishing village on Guatemala’s Pacific coast, beside a long beach of black volcanic sand. Its powerful beach breaks attract surfers; on smaller days, the village’s surf schools look after beginners.
Village de pêcheurs de la province d’Esm: Fishing village in Esmeraldas Province, beside a long beach backed by forest. Its point break, which peels at the end of the bay, is one of Ecuador’s best-known waves.
Village de pêcheurs devenu capitale du s: Fishing village turned Moroccan surf capital. The beach below the village is great for beginners, while the nearby points draw advanced surfers.
Village de pêcheurs du nord du Pérou don: Fishing village in northern Peru, home to a fast, hollow left that breaks over a rocky bottom. It works best with northwest swells during the boreal winter.
Village de pêcheurs et d’algoculteurs au: Fishing and seaweed-farming village in southwest Rote, Indonesia’s southernmost island. Offshore, the T-Land reef left peels for a long way when southern swells arrive, especially in the dry season.
Village de pêcheurs à l’ouest de Fortale: Fishing village west of Fortaleza, between colourful cliffs and dunes. The trade winds blow strongly for much of the second half of the year, with a lagoon and open sea for kitesurfing.
Village de surf aux droites de pointe su: Surf town with point-break rights over cobbles, in the heart of « Surf City ». Consistent, warm waves.
Village de surf bohème de la côte équato: A bohemian surf village on Ecuador's coast, with a fun point break and a lively atmosphere.
Village du canal de Pelješac, face à Kor: Village on the Pelješac Channel, facing Korčula, where the thermal maestral blows regularly on summer afternoons. It’s one of the Adriatic’s best-known windsurfing and kitesurfing spots.
Village isolé au bout de pistes de sable: Remote village at the end of sandy tracks, with several reef breaks. A surf adventure at the end of the world.
Remote village, long drive to get there.
Village où le récif de Ningaloo commence: Village where Ningaloo Reef starts just a few metres from the beach. Manta rays and whale sharks in season.
Village sans route ni réseau électrique,: Village with no road or electricity grid, among the dunes of a national park, reached by off-road truck. Two beaches lie on either side of the headland, and a sea lion colony occupies the rocks below the lighthouse.
Village sans voitures du golfe d’Urabá,: Car-free village in the Gulf of Urabá, near the Panamanian border, between jungle and the Caribbean Sea. Walk or take a boat to coves such as Aguacate or Sapzurro for snorkelling.
Village sans voitures sur l’île de Tinha: Car-free village on Tinharé Island, south of Salvador. The numbered beaches follow one after another; at low tide, natural pools form between the reefs.
Ville coloniale au bord d’une baie parse: Colonial city beside a bay dotted with islands and beaches, between the sea and Atlantic Forest. The calm waters are ideal for kayaking, paddleboarding and boat trips to the coves.
Ville de surf de la côte ouest irlandais: Surf town on Ireland’s west coast, near the Cliffs of Moher. The beach break welcomes beginners, while nearby reefs are for experts.
Ville natale de Kelly Slater, avec un po: Kelly Slater’s hometown, with a pier and accessible waves. The heart of the Space Coast surf scene.

À l'extrémité sud de Ninety Mile Beach,: At the southern end of Ninety Mile Beach, a series of rocky points produces left-hand waves that can connect for hundreds of metres.
À la frontière espagnole, une grande pla: At the Spanish border, a wide beach opens the bay onto the Atlantic. You can surf along the seafront; choose areas and conditions with local surf schools.
À la pleine lune, les marées sont…: At full moon, the tides are…
À l’eau, les conditions réelles priment: In the water, actual conditions always take priority: check tide times, currents, wind, flags and local guidance. A rip-current channel can carry you out to sea: stay calm, signal for help, swim parallel to the beach to get out of the current, then head to the lifeguarded area.
À l’est de l’archipel de la Sonde, les d: East of the Sunda Islands, the Alor straits stir up nutrient-rich water: walls covered in soft corals, macro life and pelagic fish. Dives usually depart from Alor Kecil or Kalabahi.
À l’extrémité de la péninsule de Gramvou: At the tip of the Gramvousa peninsula, Balos lagoon stretches out opposite Cape Tigani. A place to discover the Cretan coast while respecting access rules and protected areas.
À marée basse l'eau est loin : surveille: At low tide the water is far away: keep an eye on the incoming tide.
À marée basse, quelques centimètres suff: At low tide, just a few centimetres of water can leave you scraping the coral.
À moins d’un kilomètre du spot: Less than a kilometre from the spot
À quoi sert le leash (cordon) en surf ?: What is a surf leash for?
Ça dépend de l'endroit 🐠 ! Eaux tropical: It depends where you are 🐠! Tropical waters: turtles, colourful fish, rays, reef sharks. Temperate/cold waters: dolphins, seals, schools of fish, seabirds, kelp forests. Ask me about wildlife at a specific spot (e.g. “wildlife at Pipeline”).
Éboulements possibles : ne t’installe pa: Rockfalls are possible: don't settle at the foot of the cliffs.
Échauffe-toi avant la session et garde t: Warm up before your session and always keep an eye on the other surfers around you.
Éloigne-toi de la jetée et de l'embouchu: Stay away from the jetty and the river mouth, and avoid murky water and schools of fish.
Énormément de bateaux au mouillage en ét: Lots of boats at anchor in summer: swim in the marked area.
Épave accessible depuis la plage, posée: A wreck accessible from the beach, resting a few metres down and covered in coral: perfect for beginners or snorkelling.
Épave historique protégée : interdiction: Protected historic wreck: entering it or touching or removing anything is prohibited.
Étroit chenal entre les îles de Drawaqa: Narrow channel between the islands of Drawaqa and Naviti in the Yasawa archipelago, where manta rays come to feed during the season. Trips depart from the nearby small resorts.
Étroit chenal près de Bodø où passe l’un: Narrow channel near Bodø where one of the world’s strongest tidal currents flows, with whirlpools visible from the bridge. Between tides, diving reveals abundant life along the walls.
Évite de surfer après de fortes pluies :: Avoid surfing after heavy rain: the lagoon drains into the ocean and water quality drops.
Évite de te baigner avec des coupures ou: Avoid swimming with cuts or just after shaving.
Évite donc bijoux et montres brillantes: So avoid shiny jewellery and watches in the water.
Évite la crème solaire classique et ne m: Avoid regular sunscreen and don’t walk on the stromatolites, the very fragile living formations along the shore.
Évite la marée haute par forte houle et: Avoid high tide in big swell and check the currents near the rocks.
Évite la saison des pluies (octobre à dé: Avoid the rainy season (roughly October to December) and opt for a small-group trip early in the morning.
Évite la saison des typhons de juillet à: Avoid typhoon season from July to September.
Évite la zone du chenal portuaire à l'es: Avoid the harbour channel area to the east.
Évite les jours d’escale des paquebots,: Avoid cruise ship stopover days, and plan for the access fee requested by the customary landowners.
Île aussi utilisée pour des exercices mi: Island also used for military exercises: access is supervised; check locally.
Île aux eaux peu profondes et au vent ré: Island with shallow water and steady wind, with large lagoons in the southeast. A great place to learn in the Mediterranean.
Île basse et très ventée des Hébrides in: A low-lying, very windy island in the Inner Hebrides, nicknamed “Hawaii of the North” by windsurfers. Balevullin Beach, on the west coast, takes the Atlantic swell head-on.
Île classée au patrimoine mondial avec l: World Heritage-listed island with the southernmost coral reef in the world. Visitor numbers are limited.
Île célèbre du golfe de Naples : eaux bl: Famous island in the Gulf of Naples: blue waters, the Blue Grotto and coves to explore by kayak or while snorkeling.
Île de Micronésie réputée pour ses raies: Micronesian island known for its manta rays, seen in the channels that cut through the reef. The pin marks Colonia, where dive boats depart from.
Île de la baie de Nha Trang, au cœur de: Island in Nha Trang Bay, at the heart of Vietnam’s first marine protected area. It’s the region’s best-known spot for discovering corals and reef fish while snorkelling or on a beginner dive.
Île de la réserve nationale Pingüino de: Island in the Pingüino de Humboldt National Reserve, reached by boat from Punta de Choros. Its white-sand coves and clear but cold water can be explored with penguins and dolphins nearby.
Île des Andaman aux eaux cristallines et: Andaman island with crystal-clear waters and dream beaches like Radhanagar. Dive on pristine reefs.
Île du parc marin de Terengganu, au larg: Island in Terengganu Marine Park, off the east coast of the Malay Peninsula. White-sand beaches and fringing reefs are great for snorkelling, often with turtles.
Île du parc national Machalilla, à une q: Island in Machalilla National Park, about 40 km from Puerto López, nicknamed the “poor man’s Galápagos” for its blue-footed boobies. Snorkelling takes place above a small reef near the mooring.
Île désertique de la mer d’Arabie, balay: Desert island in the Arabian Sea, swept by the southwest monsoon from June to September.
Île isolée : soins médicaux limités, éva: Remote island: medical care is limited, and evacuation takes a long time.
Remote island, far from medical help.
Île montagneuse des Caraïbes colombienne: Mountainous Caribbean island off Colombia, at the heart of the Seaflower Biosphere Reserve and surrounded by a vast barrier reef. Manzanillo is a quiet beach in the south; dive centres head out to the reef and Crab Cay.
Île montagneuse entourée de parc marin,: Mountainous island surrounded by a marine park, with a variety of dive sites and quiet villages.
Île rocheuse en forme de cœur au large d: Heart-shaped rocky island off Murudeshwar, one of the best-known dive spots on India’s west coast. Dives take place around the rocks, among corals and reef fish.
Île très isolée : aucun caisson de recom: Very remote island: no recompression chamber nearby, and evacuation takes more than a day.
Île volcanique au large de Taitung, ento: Volcanic island off Taitung, surrounded by coral reefs. Bays such as Chaikou are great for snorkelling from shore, and divers can explore huge boulder corals.
Île volcanique cernée d'un tombant verti: Volcanic island ringed by a dizzying drop-off, famous for swirling schools of barracuda and green turtles.
Île volcanique inhabitée à environ 550 k: Uninhabited volcanic island about 550 km from the coast, in a national park listed as a World Heritage Site. It’s only accessible on a multi-day liveaboard trip, for renowned dives among schools of hammerhead sharks.
Île-montagne calcaire au large d’Olbia,: Limestone mountain island off Olbia, at the heart of the Tavolara – Punta Coda Cavallo Marine Protected Area. Granite seabeds, drop-offs and Posidonia meadows are home to groupers, barracuda and gorgonians.
Îles de jungle et de sable blanc, avec t: Jungle and white-sand islands, with turtles and blacktip sharks in the lagoon. Closed during the monsoon.
Îles désertiques face à Hurghada, dans u: Desert islands opposite Hurghada, in a marine protected area, surrounded by fringing reefs and dive sites. Day trips stop at the beaches of Giftun Kebir, such as Mahmya or Orange Bay.
Îles volcaniques cernées de récifs frang: Volcanic islands ringed by fringing reefs, surrounded by warm open water.
Îles volcaniques en plein Atlantique : e: Volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic: mild waters and dark drop-offs.
Îles volcaniques en réserve marine, clas: Volcanic islands in a marine reserve, ranked among the world’s top ten dive sites by Cousteau. Giant arches and caves.
Îlets Pigeon, au large de Bouillante : u: Îlets Pigeon, off Bouillante: a reserve made popular by Commander Cousteau. Turtles, coral and an underwater bust.
Islet accessible only at low tide.
Îlot de sable dominé par son grand phare: A sandy islet dominated by its tall metal lighthouse, in the lagoon south of Nouméa, near Boulari Pass. The surrounding reef is great for easy snorkelling; take a boat from Nouméa to get there.
Îlot isolé à une centaine de kilomètres: A remote islet about a hundred kilometres west of Key West, home to a huge 19th-century brick fort. Swim from the beach along the moat wall, where corals and fish have made themselves at home.
Îlot volcanique au large de Seogwipo, au: A volcanic islet off Seogwipo, within a marine reserve. Its walls covered in soft corals make it Jeju’s best-known dive site.
Îlots rocheux au nord de l’île Espíritu: Rocky islets north of Espíritu Santo Island, in the Gulf of California, home to a large colony of California sea lions. Snorkel or dive among the young sea lions, who are often very curious.
